name: Alvvays
label: Polyvinyl
lede: Molly Rankin wrote 'Adult Diversion' behind a smoothie shop counter, buried a snowmobile outside a PEI farmhouse, lost her demo recorder to a thief, and still ended up with Pitchfork's No. 3 album of 2022.

eras.title: From Cape Breton to Toronto, under a name that won't last
eras.text: Molly Rankin grew up on Cape Breton Island in a family of Celtic folk musicians and starts writing with Prince Edward Island guitarist Alec O'Hanley. By 2012 they're in Toronto with a keyboard player and a name they're about to lose.

years.src: Exclaim!: Alvvays, long journey to overnight success · Wikipedia: Alvvays
years.h: Molly Rankin cuts a solo EP, She, with Roy Orbison in her ear
years.p: Alec O'Hanley helps out on the record, a year before either of them has a band.
years.xp:
Rankin is the daughter of John Morris Rankin of the Cape Breton folk group [[The Rankin Family|5bda7192-a859-4365-8c51-c77894f38212]]. She grew up on the island (Wikipedia says Mabou, Exclaim! says Judique) and wrote with neighbour [[Kerri MacLellan|aa4daa19-55bc-443c-ad9e-7374d1ad06dd]] long before Alvvays existed.

Rankin and O'Hanley met at a show by [[Two Hours Traffic|7f5258b4-05aa-4b12-a386-4c1d3c48051c]], O'Hanley's band at the time. Exclaim! quotes O'Hanley on hearing her music: "This was one of those sympathetic nervous system responses where you get all tingly."

years.src: Exclaim!: Alvvays, long journey to overnight success · Wikipedia: Alvvays
years.h: Alec O'Hanley quits Two Hours Traffic, and the band moves to Toronto
years.p: With bassist Brian Murphy and drummer Phil MacIsaac, both from PEI, Molly Rankin starts over in the city and takes whatever day jobs let them tour.
years.xp:
O'Hanley told Exclaim! that after the move, "almost immediately things started to click a little more."

Before they were Alvvays they played under several names, Logos among them, then settled on Always. After a UK dream pop band turned out to own that name, Exclaim! reports the spelling changed for search-engine reasons. Wikipedia adds that another band called Always was already signed to Sony.

Rankin has described the new spelling as keeping a shred of sentiment and nostalgia.

years.src: Exclaim!: Alvvays, long journey to overnight success · Wikipedia: Alvvays
years.h: Rankin's Cape Breton neighbour Kerri MacLellan takes the keyboards
years.p: The two had written together back home before Alvvays existed, and MacLellan fills out the sound the debut is built on.
years.xp: Exclaim! dates her arrival to 2012; Wikipedia lists her among the five founding members in 2011.

eras.title: The debut gets made in Calgary and tops college radio
eras.text: Two songs written out of boredom and bad weather get the band onto blogs and then onto Polyvinyl. By August 2014 the debut sits at No. 1 on US college radio.

years.src: Wikipedia: Alvvays (album)
years.h: The debut gets made in Chad VanGaalen's studio in Calgary
years.p: The band picks VanGaalen for his work on the band Women, and records at his Yoko Eno studio.
years.xp: VanGaalen plays guitars, programming and percussion, and Wikipedia says he also suggested the band take a group name. Graham Walsh adds tracking at his Basketball4Life studio, John Agnello mixes in Brooklyn and Greg Calbi and Steve Fallone master at Sterling Sound.

years.cap: Alvvays around the release of the debut
years.src: Wikipedia: Archie, Marry Me · CBC Music: Archie, Marry Me certified gold
years.h: Rankin and O'Hanley bury a snowmobile and write 'Archie, Marry Me'
years.p: The song comes together in a snowed-in PEI farmhouse and is out as a single on April 6, 2013. Its Archie is Rankin's cousin Archie Rankin, a geologist and musician.
years.xp:
Rankin's account of the snowmobile, per Wikipedia: "We had a snowmobile to get to the road, but we ended up burying the snowmobile."

Rolling Stone later ranked it No. 28 on its list of the best songs of the 2010s. CBC Music reported the song was certified gold a decade after release, and Wikipedia specifies US certification.

years.big: "Only one or two people would come in during the day and usually only to use the washroom."
years.src: Wikipedia: Adult Diversion · Exclaim!: Alvvays, long journey to overnight success
years.h: Smoothie shop shifts give Rankin 'Adult Diversion'
years.p: Rankin on her solo shifts at a Toronto smoothie shop, where the song started. Exclaim! calls it a love song from the point of view of a drunk stalker.
years.xp:
The single came out October 28, 2013, with a Super 8 beach video. About a month later, per Wikipedia, the band signed with Canadian label Royal Mountain Records, which led to Polyvinyl in the US, who sold a limited 7 inch of it paired with 'Archie, Marry Me' to mail-order subscribers.

Rankin's own description, per Wikipedia: "That song spawned out of admiration from afar and spending a large chunk of time alone."

years.cap: Alvvays at Birthdays in Toronto, August 2014
years.src: Exclaim!: Alvvays, long journey to overnight success · Wikipedia: Alvvays
years.h: A strong SXSW brings Polyvinyl to the band
years.p: Good SXSW sets and online response to 'Adult Diversion' get the debut a US label, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: The record had been shopped before that. Alec O'Hanley told Exclaim!, "We sent our record out to a bunch of labels and no one really bit."

years.src: Wikipedia: Alvvays (album) · Wikipedia: Alvvays
yt: Archie, Marry Me live on KEXP
years.h: Three labels put out Alvvays at once
years.p: Polyvinyl in the US, Royal Mountain in Canada and Transgressive in Europe release the debut. Pitchfork gave it 7.6.
years.xp: Rolling Stone's Simon Vozick-Levinson called it an indie-pop wonder, and the record hit No. 1 on the US college chart on August 5, 2014. The album was shortlisted for the 2015 Polaris Music Prize and ranked No. 5 on Paste's best albums of 2014. Metacritic scored it 78.

eras.title: Bigger stages, darker songs
eras.text: Glastonbury and Coachella come first, then a new drummer and a second album that swaps some of the debut's sunshine for undertow. Two Juno nominations turn into a win.

years.src: Wikipedia: Alvvays
years.h: Alvvays play Glastonbury while the debut racks up nominations
years.p: The debut earns Juno nominations for Breakthrough Group and Alternative Album of the Year, and a spot on the Polaris Music Prize shortlist.
years.xp: The band plays Glastonbury in 2015, and Coachella follows in 2016, per Wikipedia. The Polaris shortlist was announced for the 2015 prize.

years.src: Wikipedia: Alvvays
yt: Full set at the CBC Music Festival, 2016
years.h: Drummer Phil MacIsaac leaves for graphic design; Sheridan Riley takes his place
years.p: The band's original drummer steps away to work in design, according to Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: In Undertow
years.h: Norman Blake of Teenage Fanclub sings on 'In Undertow'
years.p: The lead single from the second album, out June 6, 2017, has [[Norman Blake|164066ec-7360-4a94-9937-2b48fc5f7298]] on backing vocals and extra guitar.
years.xp: Rankin said the song came partly from wobbling along a shore picking up stained glass. The video, directed by Jo Garrity, puts Rankin in an astronaut helmet and won Best Editing in a Music Video at the 2017 New York City Independent Film Festival.

years.src: Wikipedia: Antisocialites
years.h: Los Angeles, upstate New York and Toronto each get a piece of Antisocialites
years.p: Alec O'Hanley and John Congleton produce, mixing Pro Tools with a TASCAM 488 8-track. Pitchfork gave it 7.3.
years.xp: Sessions ran through Kingsize Soundlabs in Los Angeles, Tarbox Road Studios in Cassadaga, New York, and Union Sound Studios in Toronto. Metacritic scored it 77, NPR's Mike Katzif called 'In Undertow' a darker spiritual sequel to their breakthrough single, and Exclaim! named it the top pop and rock album of 2017.

years.cap: Alvvays on the Antisocialites tour, April 2018
years.src: Wikipedia: Alvvays · Wikipedia: Antisocialites
years.h: Antisocialites wins the Juno for Alternative Album of the Year
years.p: Alvvays also land a Group of the Year nomination and a second Polaris shortlist, the album's, for 2018.
years.xp: 'Dreams Tonite' picked up a SOCAN Songwriting Prize nomination the same year.

eras.title: Everything that could slow a record down does
eras.text: After Antisocialites the band goes quiet. A burglary, a flood and a pandemic hold up the next record, and the bass chair changes hands.

years.src: NME: Alvvays, the only thing I know is to put my head down · Exclaim!: Alvvays Revisit Teen Spirits to Find a New Buzz · Variety: Alvvays Interview
years.h: Someone steals Rankin's demo recorder, and the basement floods the next day
years.p: Rankin's words, per Exclaim!, for the demos on the stolen recorder, among them 'Pomeranian Spinster', 'Easy On Your Own?' and 'Belinda Says'.
years.xp:
NME reported that a basement flood the day after the theft destroyed nearly all the band's gear. Exclaim! describes the recorder as holding post-Antisocialites demos. Variety adds the pandemic, which slowed everything, to the five-year gap.

The exact dates of the theft and flood are not given in the sources.

years.src: Wikipedia: Alvvays · Exclaim!: Alvvays Revisit Teen Spirits to Find a New Buzz
years.h: Founding bassist Brian Murphy is out, and Abbey Blackwell steps in
years.p: Blackwell was living in Seattle during the pandemic, per Wikipedia and Exclaim!.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates Blackwell's stint as 2021 to 2024 and describes it as a temporary replacement.

years.src: NME: Alvvays, the only thing I know is to put my head down · Variety: Alvvays Interview · Tape Op: Alvvays · Exclaim!: Alvvays Revisit Teen Spirits to Find a New Buzz
years.h: Producer Shawn Everett has the band play the whole album twice in a day
years.p: Everett runs all 14 demos back to back, with about 15 seconds between songs and 30 minutes between full takes, per NME.
years.xp:
Everett, known for work with Kacey Musgraves and the War on Drugs, talked the band out of its usual fussy approach and had them record straight to tape, according to Exclaim! and Variety. Alec O'Hanley told Tape Op, "We're more comfortable when we're uncomfortable artificially."

Sources differ on the room: NME says Sunset Sound and Tape Op says Everett's Los Angeles warehouse. The band also tracked parts in Toronto, including at Canterbury Music Co. with drummer Chris Dadge, and at the Tragically Hip's Bathouse studio in Kingston, Ontario.

eras.title: The record everybody was waiting on
eras.text: Blue Rev lands in October 2022, tops the year-end lists at Exclaim! and Stereogum, takes No. 3 at Pitchfork and wins a Juno, and 'Belinda Says' picks up a Grammy nomination.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pharmacist (song)
years.h: 'Pharmacist' ends a five-year silence
years.p: Pitchfork's Quinn Moreland called it overblown in all the right ways, and Stereogum ranked it first in its weekly best songs list.

years.src: Wikipedia: Easy On Your Own? · Tape Op: Alvvays
years.h: 'Easy On Your Own?' turns the feedback up
years.p: Producer Shawn Everett built the song from feedback, distortion and glide guitar, and the band cites My Bloody Valentine's Loveless as a reference.
years.xp: Paste compared it to [[My Bloody Valentine|8ca01f46-53ac-4af2-8516-55a909c0905e]]. The single reached No. 32 on the US Adult Alternative Airplay chart, according to Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Belinda Says
years.h: 'Belinda Says' and 'Very Online Guy' arrive together
years.p: Pitchfork's Jamieson Cox called 'Belinda Says' a heartbreaking sketch of an unexpected pregnancy and a modern power-pop classic.
years.xp: The title nods to [[Belinda Carlisle|2925aac9-5474-4030-b8a3-4151107010b2]], who per Wikipedia posted that she was flattered by the song. The track got a Grammy nomination for Best Alternative Music Performance at the 66th Grammy Awards.

years.src: Wikipedia: Blue Rev · Album of the Year: Alvvays, Blue Rev · Polyvinyl: Blue Rev is named Pitchfork's Best New Music
years.h: Blue Rev: Pitchfork 8.8, Best New Music, No. 3 of 2022
years.p: The third album arrives five years after Antisocialites, and Exclaim! and Stereogum rank it No. 1 of the year.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's review, as quoted by Polyvinyl and Album of the Year: "a triumph of power pop, a densely layered, witty, blithe, and beautiful record." Metacritic scored it 86 from 15 reviews. Paste ranked it No. 3 and Rolling Stone No. 12.

In the US it reached No. 61 and in the UK No. 27, according to Wikipedia.

years.cap: Alvvays on the Blue Rev tour
years.src: Wikipedia: Alvvays
yt: Belinda Says live, Le Trabendo Paris
years.h: A fan films 'Belinda Says' at Le Trabendo in Paris
years.p: The Blue Rev tour reaches Paris on June 4, 2023.

years.src: Wikipedia: Alvvays
years.h: Blue Rev wins the Juno and makes a third Polaris shortlist
years.p: It is the band's second Juno for Alternative Album of the Year, after Antisocialites in 2018.

years.src: Wikipedia: Alvvays
years.h: Lukas Cheung takes over on bass
years.p: Wikipedia lists Cheung as bassist from 2024, replacing Blackwell.

years.src: Wikipedia: Belinda Says · CBC Music: Archie, Marry Me certified gold
years.h: Ten years on, 'Archie, Marry Me' goes gold and 'Belinda Says' gets a Grammy nod
years.p: The nomination is for Best Alternative Music Performance at the 66th Grammys, and CBC Music reports the 2013 single passed gold certification.
